body:
## Summary

While validating tower/connector LoRA for Voxtral (#45697), the e2e run crashed at engine
init inside encoder-cache profiling with punica's
`assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M` (`vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py:291`).
Root cause there: the `mm_kwargs=None` sizing path of `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` returned
the raw encoder budget, but profiling batches maximum-size items whose per-item counts are
chunk-padded, so the rows through the wrapped connector exceeded the punica wrapper's
buffer (evidence: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45697#issuecomment-6155052085,
fixed in that PR by chunk-ceiling the bound).

That is a bug *class*, not a one-off. I swept all implementations of
`get_mm_lora_token_counts()` on `main` (26 in `vllm/model_executor/models/` + 1 in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`), checked each model's sizing branch against its processor's
dummy/profiling items and its tower/connector forward, and found **8 models where the rows
actually flowing through LoRA-wrapped tower/connector linears can exceed the wrapper budget
computed from the sizing branch** — same assert, at engine init or on the first unlucky
batch. 4 further implementations are dead code (class flag unset), and the remaining 10 are
provably safe (details below).

## Mechanism

- Sizing (engine init): `LoRAModelManager` sizes the shared tower and connector punica
  wrappers from `get_mm_lora_token_counts(modality, mm_kwargs=None,
  num_mm_embeds=encoder_budget)` — `vllm/lora/model_manager.py:280-323`. Let `B` be the
  encoder budget (`MultiModalBudget.get_encoder_budget()`, typically
  `max_num_batched_tokens`, floor `max_tokens_per_item`).
- Runtime: for every scheduled encoder item the hook is called with the item's real
  `mm_kwargs` and its placeholder count, and the per-item counts are concatenated into the
  tower/connector `LoRAMapping` — `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/lora.py:55`,
  `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2852`.
- The scheduler budgets encoder items in **placeholder-embed currency** (`Σ embeds ≤ B`),
  but the wrapped linears run in **row currency** (padded chunks, CLS tokens, batch-max
  padding, pre-unpad tiles). Whenever a legal batch's rows exceed the wrapper buffer, the
  kernel metadata can't cover `M` and the assert fires. Engine-init profiling runs
  `max_items_per_batch = min(B // max_tokens_per_item, decoder caps)` identical max-size
  items, so an under-sized bound can crash before any request (the Voxtral case).

So a sizing implementation is only correct if it upper-bounds the rows of **any**
schedulable batch — `Σ embeds ≤ B` with up to `max_num_seqs × limit_per_prompt` items — not
just `N` identical max-size items. Several implementations return the raw budget (or miss
fixed per-item overheads), which is exactly the Voxtral failure mode.

(Kernel semantics, for precision: `meta_args()` slices the prepared mapping buffer to the
layer's row count `M` (`lora_kernel_metadata.py:198`), so `M >` wrapper buffer is a hard
assert, while a *mapping* that undercounts rows ≤ buffer silently applies stale adapter
indices to the uncounted rows — a correctness bug rather than a crash. Both appear below.)

## Affected models

### 1. Ultravox — short-audio batches overflow tower and connector

`ultravox.py:741-762`. With tower/connector LoRA, every chunk's mel input is padded to the
tower's full context (`pad_audio_to_max_context`, `ultravox.py:653-662`), so each chunk
contributes a fixed **1500 tower rows / 188 connector rows** regardless of its placeholder
count, while a short audio's placeholder count is tiny (~7 embeds per second). The sizing
branch bounds chunks by `ceil(B / 188)`, which only covers batches of *full* chunks.

Arithmetic (`B = 8192`): tower buffer `= ceil(8192/188) · 1500 = 66 000`. Forty-five
1-second audios: `Σ embeds ≈ 315 ≤ 8192` (schedulable), tower rows `= 45 · 1500 = 67 500 >
66 000` → assert. Connector: `45 · 188 = 8460 > 8272`. At `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`
the threshold is **12 concurrent short audios** (`12 · 1500 = 18 000 > 11 · 1500`). This is
an ordinary ASR serving load.

### 2 & 3. Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-Omni (audio) — `conv_out` runs on chunk-padded rows

Hook: identity (`qwen3_asr.py:678-691`; `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:2361-2374`, audio
branch). The shared `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder` splits mel input into 100-frame chunks and
pads the tail chunk to 100 before the conv stack; `conv_out` (a `ReplicatedLinear`, i.e.
LoRA-wrapped) runs on the **padded** `[chunks, 13, …]` tensor →
`13 · total_chunks` rows per item (`qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:460-520`). Placeholders count
only valid positions: `13 · full_chunks + f(tail)` (`qwen3_asr.py:175-182`), so every
non-whole-second audio contributes up to 12 rows of slack that the identity bound ignores.
(The transformer and `proj1/proj2` run on the unpadded gather, so those match embeds.)

Arithmetic (`--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, so `B = 2048`): ~1.01 s audios (101 mel
frames) give 14 embeds but `2 · 13 = 26` `conv_out` rows. 79 such audios: `Σ embeds = 1106 ≤
2048`, rows `= 2054 > 2048` → assert. At `B = 8192` the same overflow needs ~316 items, i.e.
`max_num_seqs > 256`. Engine-init profiling survives only because the dummy audio is
exactly 30 s (3000 frames, a whole number of chunks).

### 4. Gemma4-MM (audio) — tower/connector run on batch-max-padded rows

Hook audio branch returns per-item `ceil(frames/4)` from the item's own (unpadded) features
(`gemma4_mm.py:2299-2305`); sizing returns the raw budget (`tower = connector =
num_mm_embeds`). But `_process_audio_input` re-pads all items in the encoder batch to the
batch max before the tower, and `embed_audio` (the connector) runs on that padded tensor —
padding is stripped only afterwards (`gemma4_mm.py:1579-1604`). Both modules contain
vLLM linears (`recursive_replace_linear` at `gemma4_mm.py:1125`; `Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder`
at `gemma4_mm.py:1119`), so both are LoRA-wrapped.

With one max-length audio (`E` embeds) batched alongside `k` short audios, the wrapped
modules see `(k+1) · E` rows while the scheduler only accounted `E + Σ eᵢ ≤ B` — for
`k ≳ B/E` the wrapper overflows and the assert fires. Below that threshold the problem is
still there, just silent: the per-item mapping (`Σ ceil(fᵢ/4)`) is shorter than the padded
`M` of any heterogeneous batch, so the padding rows pick up stale adapter indices. The
hook's per-item signature cannot express batch-max padding at all.

### 5. LLaVA — CLS token missing from the tower bound

Hook: identity (`llava.py:733-736`). vLLM's CLIP tower prepends a class embedding
(`clip.py:324`), so each 336² image runs **577** tower rows against 576 embeds. Overflow
when `(B // 576) · 577 > B`, i.e. whenever `B mod 576 < B // 576` — e.g.
`--max-num-batched-tokens 5760`: profiling runs 10 items → `5770 > 5760` → **crash at
engine init**. The default `B = 8192` escapes by residue (`8078 < 8192`). (The pixtral-HF
vision variant has no CLS and is fine.)

### 6. LLaVA-NeXT — sizing ignores tiles, CLS and un-padding

Runtime counts are exact (`tiles · 577` / `tiles · 576`, `llava_next.py:612-629`), but the
`mm_kwargs=None` branch returns `(B, B)`. Anyres un-padding makes placeholder counts
*smaller* than tile rows for non-square images, so row/embed ratios up to ~1.9 are legal.
Verified against the real HF processor (`llava-hf/llava-v1.6-mistral-7b-hf`):

| image | tiles | embeds | tower rows | connector rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 672×672 (dummy) | 5 | 2928 | 2885 | 2880 |
| 336×500 | 3 | 1476 | 1731 | 1728 |
| 500×336 | 3 | 1464 | 1731 | 1728 |

Five 336×500 images: `Σ embeds = 7380 ≤ 8192`, tower `5 · 1731 = 8655 > 8192`, connector
`8640 > 8192` → assert. Profiling is safe only because the square dummy's ratio happens to
be < 1.

### 7. LLaVA-NeXT-Video — CLS token again

`llava_next_video.py:496-520` inverts the 2×2 pooling (`frames · 576` tower rows) but CLIP
runs `frames · 577`. Tower buffer `= (8192 // 144) · 576 = 32 256`; seven 8-frame videos:
`Σ embeds = 8064 ≤ 8192`, rows `= 56 · 577 = 32 312 > 32 256` → assert on any
budget-saturating video batch.

### 8. BLIP-2 — sizing branch asserts on the budget itself

`blip2.py:689-706` does `assert num_mm_embeds % num_query_tokens == 0` on the **budget**.
Any config where `B` isn't a multiple of 32 (e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 5000`) raises
`AssertionError` *inside wrapper sizing* at engine init. The bound should floor instead
(`B // 32` items), as InternVL does.

## Safe implementations (for contrast — these get it right)

- **InternVL / H2OVL / Mllama4 / Idefics3**: tiles are uniform, embeds are exact per-tile
  multiples, and the CLS (+1) is accounted (`internvl.py:906-918`,
  `mllama4.py:1255-1268`) — `Σ rows ≤ bound` holds for every legal batch.
- **Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL / Qwen3-Omni (vision) / GLM-4.1V / Keye / dots.ocr /
  Pixtral (native)**: varlen ViTs (no CLS, no batch padding) with processor-enforced
  merge-divisible grids, so `tower = merge² · embeds` is exact.
- **Gemma3 / PaliGemma**: fixed-size SigLIP crops, exact ratios.
- **LFM2-VL, DeepSeek-V4 VL**: varlen towers; bounds can only over-provision.
- **Gemma4-MM (image)**: sizing already ceils to whole soft-token groups.

Inert (hook implemented but `supports_tower_connector_lora` is not set, so nothing sizes or
maps today): `bailing_moe_v3_vl`, `cohere_compass`, `moondream3`, `openvla`. Note if
Moondream3's flag is ever flipped, its overlapping-crop encoder (729 rows per crop vs a
fixed 730-embed placeholder) overflows immediately — worth a comment before anyone enables
it.

## Proposed fixes

Short term, per model (mirroring the Voxtral fix, #45697 commit c553427):

1. **BLIP-2**: replace the assert with floor division. One-liner.
2. **LLaVA / LLaVA-NeXT-Video**: account the CLS token in the sizing bound
   (`(B // per_item_embeds) · (per_item_rows)`), like InternVL's `+1`.
3. **LLaVA-NeXT**: bound by worst legal row/embed ratio from the grid config instead of raw
   `B` (or `max_tiles · 577 · (B // min_embeds_per_item)`).
4. **Ultravox**: slack-aware bound. Per batch, `Σ ceil(eᵢ/188) ≤ B/188 + num_items`, so
   sizing with `(ceil(B/188) + max_num_seqs · limit_per_prompt)` chunks (× 1500 tower / 188
   connector rows) is sound. (Voxtral is immune to this variant because its placeholder
   counts are themselves chunk-padded — every item's embeds are a multiple of 375.)
5. **Qwen3-ASR / Qwen3-Omni audio**: move the valid-position gather *before* `conv_out`
   (it is a per-position linear, so masking first is semantics-preserving) — then rows ==
   embeds and the identity bound becomes exact.
6. **Gemma4 audio**: strip padding before `embed_audio` (also per-position). The HF-side
   tower's internal batch padding can't be expressed per-item, so it needs either an
   unpadded path or a batch-aware bound.

Longer term, central (this keeps recurring — see also the open per-model hook PRs #53149,
#58658, #54832, #51949, #61470 which reviewers must re-check for the same conditions):

- **Document the contract** on `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` (`interfaces.py:426`): the
  runtime path must return exactly the flattened rows entering wrapped modules *including
  every padding the forward introduces*, and the `mm_kwargs=None` path must upper-bound
  **any** schedulable batch (`Σ embeds ≤ num_mm_embeds`, item count ≤
  `max_num_seqs × limit`), not just identical max-size items.
- **Fail with context instead of a triton assert**: at mapping-build time
  (`gpu/mm/lora.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`) check `Σ rows` against the wrapper budget and
  raise a descriptive error naming the model and hook.
- Optionally, size wrappers centrally as `max_items_per_batch × hook(dummy max item)`
  (always sound, costs buffer memory), or teach the encoder scheduler to budget in tower-row
  currency. Happy to hear which direction the maintainers prefer.

I'm glad to send the per-model fixes as one or two PRs (with CPU-runnable regression tests
pinning each model's profiling/batch-shape case, in the style of the Voxtral tests in
#45697) once there's agreement on the approach.

## How this was found / validated

Code analysis of all 27 hook implementations on `main` (commit 8a8e2baa02), cross-checked
against each model's processor dummy-input builder and tower/connector forward; LLaVA-NeXT
numbers validated by running the real HF processor on CPU; the Voxtral instance of the
class was reproduced and fixed on an A100 in #45697. No other GPU repros were run — the
arithmetic above says exactly which batch shapes trip each model, and I can run targeted
repros on request. Analysis was AI-assisted; all findings were manually reviewed against
the cited code.

comments.body: IMO it is better to not put a lot of different issue in one. It would be better to have standalone issue for every case and if needed have a tracking issue the reference to all standalone issues.

title: [Bug]: enable_tower_connector_lora: get_mm_lora_token_counts() under-sizes punica wrappers in 8 models (startup/runtime token_lora_mapping asserts)
